title: Learner 01 | Day 150: Read models, denormalization, and consistency
body:
## Goal

Read models, denormalization, and consistency

## Implementation contract

**File:** `src/learnforge/specializations/learner_01/experience/evaluation.py`

**Method/unit:** `compare_with_baseline`

**Why here:** This is inside your owned AI/ML capability and the named layer. Model/data SDK details stay in adapters, rules in core, and commands/results in experience. It plugs into the same shared project architecture as other capabilities.

**Inputs and expected outputs:** Replaying an event does not double count; delayed events show a freshness marker; rebuild reproduces counts.

**Boundaries:** Keep the change inside the owned capability and preserve accepted behavior.

## Research hints

1. Research **Read models, denormalization, and consistency**. Which rule explains your named unit’s behavior?
2. Search `site:postgresql.org/docs Read models denormalization and consistency`; use [PostgreSQL tutorial](https://www.postgresql.org/docs/current/tutorial.html) for the relevant small section.
3. Predict one changed input/timing case, run it, and explain each changed value before applying the finding.

## Done

- [ ] Demonstrate this unit’s normal and boundary/failure cases in the working feature.
- [ ] Show the actual run and explain one changed case using concrete values.

**Question of the Day:** When would optimistic concurrency be preferable to holding a database lock?

**Review with @GlidingScorpion:** run the named unit; show actual output and each relevant line’s purpose, before/after values and project contribution.
